issues.legal_issue: A bench hearing an intra-court appeal may reconsider a single judge’s findings when resolving a mixed question of law and fact involving the construction of documents.
material_facts: A temple sued for title to agricultural land, possession, and mesne profits, and the trial court dismissed the suit.
The single judge, hearing an appeal from the trial court, construed two documents as showing that a grant was personal to the temple’s priest and upheld the dismissal.
In an intra-court appeal, a later bench reconsidered the documents alongside the surrounding circumstances and concluded that the grant was intended for the temple.
The challenge to that reconsideration argued that the later bench could not disturb the single judge’s factual finding.
issues.conclusion: The later bench was empowered to reconsider the documents, and it committed no error by reaching a different conclusion about the intended recipient of the grant.
issues.legal_principle: An intra-court appeal is ordinarily an appeal in which the later bench acts as a court correcting the High Court’s own order and exercises the same jurisdiction as the single bench. It differs from an appeal against a subordinate court’s order, in which the High Court acts as a court of error. The construction of documents that presents a mixed question of law and fact falls within the later bench’s powers.

predicates.intra_court_appeal: A bench of the same court hears an appeal from an order made by that court’s single judge.
predicates.document_construction_is_mixed_question_: The issue before the later bench requires construing documents in a way that involves both law and fact.

issues.definition: When a same-court appeal concerns document construction involving both law and fact, the later bench may reconsider that construction.
